title: (possible dupe but better sound) What does Enterprise Ready MCP mean? — Tobin South, WorkOS
talk_summary: Tobin South (WorkOS) walks through the lifecycle of an MCP server from local demo to public SaaS to enterprise sale, arguing that auth, access control, audit logging, and DLP are the real blockers, not hosting. He highlights that passing authorization scopes between chained AI workloads is the hardest unsolved problem.

takeaways.technique: Scoped auth + admin privilege tiers on internal tool endpoints
takeaways.what_they_do: Every MCP server gets login, scoped permissions, and an admin tier so no caller can over-invoke a tool; internal deployments sit behind a VPC/gateway.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You should not have an external API that is unauthenticated that has no access controls on it.

takeaways.technique: Input validation against prompt injection at tool boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: Validate inputs at the MCP server before acting, specifically to block prompt-injection attacks that arrive through tool calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're going to end up needing uh input validation so that no one prompt injection attacks your goats.

takeaways.technique: Explicit scope passing between chained agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that A2A-style agent-to-agent calls pass intent 'mostly in vibes' and rely on model alignment; real authorization scopes must be carried explicitly between workloads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you are just telling an agent mostly in vibes what it should or shouldn't do

takeaways.technique: Audit logging shaped to compliance requirements
takeaways.what_they_do: Enterprise AI workloads need audit logs meeting specific regulatory schemas (e.g., GDPR), which standard app logs don't satisfy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your audit logs that exist normally have to fit a very specific set of requirements which are not well supported widely

takeaways.technique: Elicitation for missing input instead of guessing
takeaways.what_they_do: New MCP RFC lets a model call back to a human for missing details rather than proceeding on assumptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when your model doesn't know what to do, it knows that it should ask a human being
